chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who walked between As-Safa and Al-Marwah for eight paces (shawat), what is upon him? He said: 'If it was by mistake, he discards one and counts seven.'

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: Shawat (plural of shawt, meaning paces or circuits)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk)
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Tawaf ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim makes a mistake in the number of circuits during Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of leniency (*rukhas*) in ritual acts, distinguishing between intentional transgression and unintentional error (*khata'*) in the seven circuits of Sa'i. It underscores the validity of the core ritual even when minor mechanical errors occur, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on ease for the pilgrim. This specific legal nuance is crucial for understanding the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the completeness of Hajj rituals.
